# DocketDiff — FMCSA authority and insurance changes for the carriers you use (Windows, one payment a year)

Watch the carriers you use for changes that appear in public FMCSA tables, once a day, on your own Windows computer.
It shows the rows it found for your carriers, keeps them with your decisions, and writes a record for each load you enter.
Your carrier list stays on your computer.

## Who it is for

Freight brokers in the United States, including 3PLs that arrange truckload or LTL shipments as brokers (within the definition of a broker in 49 CFR 371.2).

## Start in three steps

1. Double-click `dm11-authority-watch.exe` in the `DocketDiff` folder.
2. One screen says what will be read and from where. Press Enter. (Measured on 2026-10-20: the first read took 63 seconds.)
3. Paste your carriers' numbers — MC, FF or MX docket numbers and USDOT numbers, mixed, one carrier per line — and press
   Enter on an empty line. The rows the public tables hold for them since 2026-05-18 appear.

On the next days, double-click again: it reads what is new and shows the rows first read since the previous read.
Numbers without MC, FF, MX or DOT in front are not guessed: the program asks what they are. A CSV file can be added from
the same window. Nothing has to be typed in a Command Prompt; the commands still exist for those who want them.

## What it does (only what is backed by an implementation and a test)

- Once a day, read four public FMCSA tables from data.transportation.gov, from rows dated 2026-05-18 on.
- Compare them with your carrier list on this computer. Docket numbers are matched exactly after the forms
  `MC-012345`, `MC012345` and `mc 12345` are written the same way; one number is never searched for inside another.
- Watch each docket (MC, FF or MX number) separately, and group what you see by USDOT number. When you add a carrier,
  the rows for it since 2026-05-18 that were already read are shown at once.
- Show each row in the table's own words, with a heading and a level (ALERT or INFO) added by this program.
- Say "No change seen in the public tables from 2026-05-18 to <date>" only when the tables were read completely within the
  last 29 hours and their newest dated rows are recent. Otherwise it says up to which date the tables were checked,
  and why it cannot say more.
- Keep what it read, your decisions and your transaction records in a database that refuses to change or delete them.
- Write a carrier check record (an HTML page) for each transaction you enter, and keep its SHA-256 in the history.
- Export your records as CSV files that open safely in Excel.
- Run with sample tables and sample carriers (`demo`) without using the network.

## What it does not do

- It does not tell you a carrier's current operating authority or insurance status. Many carriers have no row in these
  tables; no row means only that no change was published there since 2026-05-18.
- It does not prevent fraud, and it does not make your records complete under 49 CFR 371.3.
- It does not send your carrier list, notes, decisions or transactions anywhere. DM11 receives nothing.
- It does not read phone numbers, addresses, names, insurance company names or policy numbers from the tables.
- It does not email you. It reads only when the program is open on a computer that is on.

## Where it goes on the network

Only `https://data.transportation.gov` — the four tables below and their descriptions. Nothing else, and no redirect is followed.
The request text holds the table id, a date and a page position; it never holds your carrier numbers.
As with any website, data.transportation.gov can see that this computer read the tables (its IP address and the time).

- Motus AuthHist - All With History (`yu5v-wbh6`): `docket_number`, `usdot_number`, `op_auth_type`, `op_auth_status`, `reason`, `status_change_date` — filtered on `status_change_date`
- Motus RevokeSuspend – All With History (`wb4f-neki`): `docket_number`, `usdot_number`, `op_auth_type`, `order1_type_desc`, `order1_serve_date`, `order1_effective_date` — filtered on `order1_serve_date`
- Motus Insur - All With History (`c5y8-a4uz`): `docket_number`, `usdot_number`, `ins_type_code`, `effective_date`, `trans_date` — filtered on `trans_date`
- Motus InsHist - All With History (`3uet-3z4i`): `docket_number`, `usdot_number`, `ins_type_code`, `filing_status_reason`, `effective_date`, `cancl_effective_date` — filtered on `cancl_effective_date`

## Carriers watched and the licence

Up to 5 carriers are watched free, with no time limit. A licence is a file for one year, bought with one payment, that
watches more. There is no subscription and no automatic renewal: to keep watching more after a year, buy the next year.

- A year runs from the payment date to the same day of the same month the next year (a year that starts on 29 February
  ends on 28 February).
- A notice appears on screen 30 days and 7 days before the end, with where to buy the next year.
- After the end, watching continues for 14 days. After that, up to 5 carriers are watched, as without a licence.
  If your list is longer, you choose which 5 (menu: "Choose which carriers to watch", or `dm11-authority-watch keep <id> <id> ...`);
  until you choose, watching is stopped and the screen says so. Carriers you do not choose stay in your list; for them the
  program shows only the rows it read while they were watched. Your records stay readable and can be exported, and you
  can still edit your carrier list (up to the size of your last licence).
- Buying the next year adds one year to the later of the current end and today, so buying early loses no days. Adding the
  same receipt number again does not extend anything. A smaller licence takes effect after the current one ends.
- The date used is the latest of this computer's clock, the newest record, the newest dated row in the tables and the
  date the table server sends. Setting the computer's clock back does not move it back. This computer's clock (and records
  written with it) is counted only up to 2 days after the date the table server last sent, so a clock set ahead does
  not bring the end early and is not kept. If the program has not been opened for a while, the date is corrected by the
  first answer from the table server when it reads.

This licence is a record of a purchase, not a lock. It is not tamper-evident: the program is built from the Python standard library only, which has no public-key signatures. The licence is never checked over a network. It covers one year from the payment date, up to the same day of the same month the next year.

   type the receipt number and the payment date. (Or in a Command Prompt in the program folder:
   `dm11-authority-watch licence install watch_licence.json --receipt <receipt number> --paid-on <YYYY-MM-DD>`.)

## Size and time (measured)

On the UTC day 2026-10-20, the first read took 62.8 seconds and 28 requests, all to data.transportation.gov. It read Motus AuthHist - All With History 109,096; Motus InsHist - All With History 52,915; Motus Insur - All With History 57,303; Motus RevokeSuspend – All With History 31,367
rows (every count matched the count the table reported). Rows that were identical in every column read were kept once:
247,820 rows. The database was 123 MB as written by that read, and 102 MB when the same rows were stored
again with this build. Later reads only fetch the last few days.

## Known limitations

- The tables cover changes from 2026-05-18 on. Earlier history is not read.
- Insurance policy history rows carry no date of publication; rows whose cancellation date is more than 10 days before the
  previous read are not seen.
- If the computer is off or the program is closed, nothing is read; the screen says up to which date the tables were checked.
- Anyone who has a licence file and a receipt number can add it. The licence is a record of a purchase, not a lock.
- After a long absence, the program learns the date from the first answer of the table server (a table's description).
  If watching should stop by then, it stops there and reads no rows.
- Screens are in English only.

## Not measured

- Whether a carrier's row appears in these tables at all before a change (coverage of carriers by the tables).
- How the tables behave on a federal holiday; a quiet day may be shown as "stale suspected".
- Behaviour of the packaged program on the network: the packaged program was run with sample tables only.
- The format of Stripe receipt numbers: the program accepts letters, digits and dashes (4 to 64 characters).

### If Windows shows a warning

This program is not signed by a publisher. The first time it runs, Windows may show "Windows protected your PC".

1. Before you run it, check the file. In PowerShell in the program folder, run `Get-FileHash .\dm11-authority-watch.exe` and compare the hash with `9d4cc0c829f2a45ace4881458615ed37bcb479abbd2f057cbf7f09430fc57606` (PowerShell shows it in capital letters; that is the same value).
2. If they are the same, choose "More info", then "Run anyway".

- If Smart App Control is on, Windows blocks programs that are not signed, and this program does not run. We do not ask you to turn Smart App Control off. You can find this out with the free allowance before you buy.
- Some antivirus programs may block or remove a program that is not signed. If the hash is the same, you can report it to your antivirus vendor as a false positive.
